scope: Reduced classical X/phi scalar pilot only. Same-session AI review; not outside replication; no validation, exclusion or new theory.

verdicts.claim: Conjugate/normal RMS ratio 0.44-1.70 in the count-dominant IR (shells 1-3, k<=1.57)
verdicts.ours_reproduction_bitwise: all three RESPONSE npz regenerated with max relative difference 0.0
verdicts.why: Codex's single white-noise probe per case has normal-channel probe-to-probe differences of 61%/31%/24% in shells 1-3 (seed 7 vs 11, same field). 1.704 (s20 shell 1) and 0.633 (s20.44 shell 1) are single-probe excursions (+30%, +26%). The phase dependence (x2.6 in shell 1) is real. [C]

verdicts.note: Z+ + Z- = dG_N/dt(0) = 1 for ANY background (equal-time commutator / f-sum). It tests the finite transform only and carries no quasiparticle information. [D]

verdicts.claim: Definitions of the normal and conjugate channels; probe normalisation
verdicts.detail: delta psi = G_N p + G_A conj(p), p = kick of d psi/ds = pi1 + i pi2; normal = .5(R00+R11+i(R10-R01)), conjugate = .5(R00-R11+i(R10+R01)); identity error 1.1e-15. The estimator is a |src|^2-weighted stochastic shell trace, sum_k q_k conj(src_k)/sum|src_k|^2; initial slope 0.986-0.997 consistent with omega^2 = k^2 + Hartree m^2. [D/C]

verdicts.claim: The medium response is a matrix; normal and conjugate mix strongly; this does not exclude quasiparticles
verdicts.verdict: CONFIRMED, with NEW resolution by momentum
verdicts.UV_k_ge_2.6: Floquet-HFB Bogoliubov (measured eccentric orbit + spatially averaged Hessian incl. anisotropic fluctuations) reproduces pole positions to <=2.3% (<=0.6% for k>=4.7), the conjugate/normal ratio to typically 5-15% (range -27%..+21%), e.g. shell 15: 0.34/0.26 vs measured 0.30-0.32/0.25. Extra widths Gamma 0.15-0.47 (Gamma/omega 0.017-0.088). Narrow matrix quasiparticles. [C]
verdicts.IR_k_le_2: Not mean-field quasiparticles: 2-pole residual 24-38% (model 11-17%), peaks 8-20% below HFB, normal-channel L2 error of every homogeneous closure 0.7-1.3 over 0-6; kicks at k=0.52 scatter out of the kicked mode at amplitude ratio 0.58 (t<1), 1.07 (1-2), 1.3-1.4 (t>2). [C]
verdicts.condensate_only_BdG: Parametrically unstable for k^2 <= 7.1 (Floquet rates 0.19-0.82 per unit s); errors 250-4000%. [C]
verdicts.circular_Bogoliubov: IR ratio 0.71-0.80 (k=0.52), 0.54-0.60, 0.36-0.45; UV 0.055-0.080 vs measured 0.25-0.32: misses the static anomalous term of the eccentric orbit. [D/C]

verdicts.claim: Coherent counting: radial action J_r (slow matching) differs from the lab-frequency statistic
verdicts.detail: J_r is the k=0 radial-branch (antiparticle-like) quasiparticle action of the circular condensate with the same charge. Same-window J_r/lab: 14-24: 0.6237/0.6075 (+2.7%); 24-34: 0.4798/0.4760 (+0.8%); 0-6: 1.6815/1.6657 (+0.95%); Codex initial orbit 1.763725/1.737788 (+1.5%). [D/C]

verdicts.claim: NEW: X-bar budget per net charge in quasiparticle bases
verdicts.circular_reference_basis: Radial-branch quasiparticles are 97-99.8% lab antiparticles (|v/u| 0.019-0.050). Waves 1.1465-1.1508 vs lab 1.1442 (+0.2-0.6%); with coherent J_r: 1.770-1.775 vs 1.7517 (+1.1-1.3%). [E]
verdicts.floquet_HFB_basis: This basis reproduces the measured UV response. Its quasiparticles are particle-antiparticle mixtures (lab A-/W 0.30-0.70, charge per action up to +-0.4); orbit-averaged static anisotropy dH 2.9-3.5 gives X<->X-bar conversion half-periods ~8-16 in s for one mode, shorter than the measured span (s 14-34). Inverting the measured (A-, A+) per shell onto Floquet branches is ill-conditioned (condition number up to 50 and 494; negative actions). X-bar is not a quasiparticle quantum number here. [C/E]
verdicts.identity: A+ - A- = Q (spectral charge ratio 1.0002), so A- = (S - Q)/2 with S = sum |omega| P. S per net charge is 4.483-4.504 over all 18 windows. The constancy of the X-bar budget is the constancy of S. [D/C]

verdicts.claim: NEW: implication for the kinetic closure
verdicts.detail: UV (k >= 2.6, shells 5-15) carries 17% (s 14-24) / 15% (s 24-34) of the wave X-bar action: a condensate + Floquet-HFB quasiparticle (ZNG-type, relativistic, with anomalous terms) closure is justified there at Gamma/omega <= 0.09. IR (k <= 2.1, shells 1-4) carries 83% / 85% of the wave action, plus the coherent part: a momentum-diagonal Boltzmann/ZNG closure is not justified. Needed: matrix (Nambu) 2PI/Kadanoff-Baym at NLO with an inhomogeneous condensate, or the classical-statistical field itself. The kinetic input should carry Q (exact) and S, or the matrix correlators, not a scalar n_Xbar. [A]
